title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: connect agents to the remote Work IQ MCP server
summary: Hold: granting WorkIQAgent.Ask does not let a client reach everything the user can reach; Work IQ also restricts accessible resources and evaluates tenant policy. The documented controls, consumption licensing and roadmap details check out, but the spending-policy rollback advice also needs the qualification that another policy can still provide access.

claims.claim: The sources do not state that this remote API capability changes existing behaviour for users who do nothing.

claims.quote: For developers, these controls mean an MCP request can fail because of tenant policy even when the user is authenticated and the app has the required OAuth permission.

Keep the permission description but qualify its resources as 'accessible to Work IQ agents and scoped to the signed-in user', as stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/permissions. The following bullet can continue to explain tenant-policy restrictions.

Use https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits#edit-spending-policy as docs and add that source.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn's rollback instructions say removing Work IQ API or the cohort from its spending policy stops that cohort without tenant-wide blocking.
